name: Kingdom of Tahiti 1788-1842
description: The Kingdom of Tahiti emerged under the Pōmare dynasty in the late 18th century, consolidating control over the island and nearby territories. It engaged in diplomacy with European powers and adopted Christianity. In 1842 France imposed a protectorate, and in 1880 Tahiti was formally annexed, ending its sovereignty.

name: Kingdom of Bora Bora 1788-1888
description: The Kingdom of Bora Bora emerged in the late 18th century as a sovereign Polynesian monarchy within the Society Islands. It maintained independence while engaging in limited diplomacy with European powers. Despite earlier recognition of autonomy, France annexed Bora Bora in 1888, ending its sovereignty and incorporating it into French Polynesia.

name: Kingdom of Raiatea-Tahaa c.1720-1888
description: Raiatea-Tahaa was a sacred and political center of Polynesia, remaining independent after Tahiti became a French protectorate. Its rulers resisted annexation for decades. In 1888 France used military force to suppress resistance and formally annexed the islands, ending the kingdom’s sovereignty and integrating them into French Polynesia.

name: Kingdom of Tonga 1875-1900
description: After the 1875 Constitution promulgated by King George Tupou I, Tonga became a centralized constitutional monarchy with defined laws, parliament and land system. It maintained internal sovereignty while navigating foreign pressure. In 1900 Tonga signed a Treaty of Friendship with Britain, becoming a protected state but not a colony.

name: United Kingdom of Fiji 1871-1874
description: Established in 1871 under King Cakobau, the United Kingdom of Fiji unified several chiefdoms into a constitutional monarchy with a parliament dominated by European settlers. Financial instability and internal tensions weakened the state. In 1874 Cakobau ceded sovereignty to Britain, ending Fijian independence and beginning colonial rule.

name: Fiji (1970-present)
description: Fiji gained independence from the United Kingdom on October 10, 1970. Originally a Kingdom under Seru Epenisa Cakobau before colonial rule, it remained a Dominion until 1987, when a series of military coups led to the declaration of a republic and its temporary withdrawal from the Commonwealth. Despite subsequent political instability and further coups, Fiji has transitioned back to a parliamentary democracy, balancing its diverse indigenous and Indo-Fijian heritage.

name: Kingdom of Rarotonga 1858-1888
description: Founded in 1858 under Queen Makea Takau, the Kingdom of Rarotonga unified local ariki into a centralized monarchy influenced by missionaries. It maintained internal autonomy while engaging with foreign powers. In 1888 it became a British protectorate, and in 1893 it was incorporated into the Cook Islands Federation, ending its independent rule.

name: Kingdom of Samoa 1858/1873-1899
description: The Kingdom of Samoa developed from mid-19th century attempts to centralize power under a Tafaʻifa king, formalized in 1873. Rival chiefly factions and foreign intervention destabilized the monarchy. The 1899 Tripartite Convention between Germany, Britain and the United States partitioned the islands and formally abolished the Samoan monarchy, ending the kingdom.

name: Samoa (1962-present)
description: Samoa became the first small island state in the Pacific to achieve independence on January 1, 1962, ending decades of New Zealand administration. Formerly known as Western Samoa, the nation officially dropped the 'Western' from its name in 1997. It operates as a parliamentary democracy that uniquely integrates 'Fa'amatai'—the traditional chief system—into its political framework, maintaining a stable balance between ancestral customs and modern governance.

name: Kingdom of Huahine 1815-1895
description: The Kingdom of Huahine emerged in 1815 under the Teururai dynasty after regional conflicts in the Society Islands. It remained independent despite French expansion in Tahiti. In 1888 it became a French protectorate, and in 1895 France formally annexed the island, ending its sovereignty and integrating it into French Polynesia.

name: Kingdom of Niue 1875-1900
description: The Kingdom of Niue formed in 1875 when island chiefs established the title of Patu-iki to unify the clans and manage foreign relations. Seeking protection from rival powers, Niue requested British oversight. In 1900 it became a British protectorate, ending its full sovereignty, and in 1901 it was annexed under New Zealand administration.
